own_solution.law: Snell's law at entry: sin r = sin 40 / n; meridional zig-zag path length L / cos r travelled at speed c/n; t = n L / (c cos r). TIR check: angle at side 90 - r with sin = cos r = 0.934 > 1/n = 0.556.
assumptions: ray entering at centre of end face is meridional
non-dispersive glass, single group/phase speed c/n
side reflections lossless and do not change path length per unit axial length

notes: sin r = 0.357104, cos r = 0.934065; t = 3.6/(3e8*0.934065) = 12.847 ns. With rod at 3.3 m: t = 5.94/(2.802195e8) = 21.198 ns. Diameter enters the zig-zag geometry (reflection count, segment length) but cancels from total path length, hence C. Earlier-run lengthening (TE2F0, TACC7) has no path to the present run; could also be read as K-like temporal irrelevance, but I classify D. 1.3 m sentences all state 1.3 m; short-length sentences consistently give no number; diameter sentences both 2.5 cm. The 'length as first cut' sentence keeps the lengthening sentences non-contradictory.
